text: When you design a REST API, clear structure matters. Start by choosing simple, meaningful endpoints that describe your resources, such as /users or /orders. Use the correct HTTP methods and return proper status codes, like 200 for success or 404 when something is missing, so clients understand what happened. Good documentation is essential: it should explain every endpoint, its parameters, and example responses. Finally, plan for change by using versioning, for example /v1/users, so older apps keep working while you improve the API. These practices make your API easier to use, test, and maintain over time.
